stories.text: Constantinople has fallen to Sultan Mehmed. Greek scholars are fleeing west with their books.
A Genoese sailor in the service of Castile has sailed west across the Ocean Sea.
Portuguese ships have rounded Africa and reached India.
Sultan Selim's Ottoman army has taken Cairo. Egypt now answers to Istanbul.
The last ship of Magellan's fleet has come home, having sailed around the world.
A canon of Frombork, Copernicus, prints a book that puts the Sun at the centre.
The Holy League has beaten the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto.
In Padua, Galileo has turned a spyglass on the Moon and seen mountains.
Spain orders every Morisco out of the kingdom.
Peace is signed at Lodi. Milan, Venice and Florence stop fighting, for now.
Cosimo de' Medici is dead. The Signoria names him Father of his Country.
Lorenzo de' Medici, twenty years old, takes up his father's place.
Verrocchio's gilded ball is raised onto the lantern of the Duomo.
Duke Galeazzo Maria Sforza is stabbed to death in the church of Santo Stefano.
Giuliano de' Medici is murdered in the Duomo at Mass. Lorenzo escaped, wounded. The conspirators have been taken.
War with the Pope and Naples after the Pazzi plot. Bread is dearer.
Lorenzo sails to Naples to make peace with King Ferrante.
War between Venice and Ferrara. The price of salt rises in the market.
Plague in Milan. The Duke's health office shuts the gates.
Lorenzo the Magnificent is dead at Careggi.
Rodrigo Borgia is Pope, as Alexander VI.
King Charles of France rides into Italy with his army. Piero de' Medici has fled Florence.
A new pox is spreading through the armies at Naples. They call it the French disease.
Friar Savonarola's boys burn mirrors, cards and paintings in the Piazza.
Savonarola is put to death in the Piazza della Signoria.
The French have taken Milan. Duke Ludovico has fled to the Emperor.
Michelangelo's giant David is set up before the Palazzo della Signoria.
Pope Julius lays the first stone of a new St Peter's.
The League of Cambrai makes war on Venice.
The Medici are back in Florence with Spanish troops.
Cardinal Giovanni de' Medici is Pope, as Leo X. Bonfires all night.
The Senate orders the Jews of Venice to live in the Ghetto Nuovo.
The French king is taken prisoner at Pavia.
The Emperor's soldiers have sacked Rome. The Pope is shut in Castel Sant'Angelo.
Florence surrenders after a long siege. The Medici return as dukes.
Duke Alessandro de' Medici is murdered by his cousin. Cosimo, seventeen, takes his place.
The bishops gather at Trent for a council of the Church.
Pope Paul IV orders the Jews of Rome into a walled ghetto.
Peace at Cateau-Cambrésis. Spain holds Milan and Naples.
The Ottoman siege of Malta has failed. The Knights hold Birgu.
Grand Master de Valette lays the first stone of a new city, Valletta.
The Pope makes Cosimo de' Medici Grand Duke of Tuscany.
Plague in Venice. Titian is dead of it, they say.
Plague in Milan. Archbishop Borromeo walks barefoot through the streets.
The Pope's new calendar: ten days are skipped this October.
Famine. The grain office rations bread.
Giordano Bruno is put to death in the Campo de' Fiori.
Galileo's Starry Messenger is in every bookshop.
The new St Peter's is consecrated.
Plague in the cities of the north. The health boards shut the houses.
Galileo is made to kneel before the Inquisition in Rome.
The fishermen of Naples rise with Masaniello against the fruit tax.
The lords take up arms at St Albans: York against Lancaster.
Edward of York is crowned king after Towton.
William Caxton has set up a printing press at Westminster.
King Richard is dead at Bosworth. Henry Tudor is king.
A new sickness, the sweat, kills in a day.
King Henry VIII is crowned.
Parliament makes the king Supreme Head of the Church in England.
The king's men are closing the monasteries.
A Great Bible in English is to be set in every church.
King Henry is dead. The boy Edward is king.
Queen Mary is crowned. The Mass is back.
Queen Mary is dead. Elizabeth is queen.
James Burbage has built a playhouse called the Theatre at Shoreditch.
The Spanish Armada is scattered in the Channel.
Plague in London. The playhouses are shut.
A wet year and a failed harvest. Bread is dear.
The Lord Chamberlain's Men have built the Globe on Bankside.
The Earl of Essex rode into London in rebellion and failed.
Queen Elizabeth is dead. King James of Scotland comes south.
A plot to blow up Parliament is found. Barrels of powder under the Lords.
The King's new Bible in English is printed.
A ship called the Mayflower has sailed for Virginia.
King James is dead. Charles is king, and plague is in London.
The King has raised his standard at Nottingham. Civil war.
King Charles has been put to death at Whitehall.
Isabel of Castile has married Fernando of Aragon.
Castile's army has taken Alhama. War has come to the kingdom.
Granada has surrendered. Sultan Muhammad has handed the keys of the Alhambra to the Catholic kings.
The Catholic kings order every Jew out of their kingdoms.
Rising in the Albaicín against forced baptisms.
The Moriscos of the Alpujarras have risen against the king.
The last Marinid sultan has been killed in Fez.
The Wattasids rule in Fez.
Refugees from Granada are building new houses in Fez.
The Saadi sharif has taken Fez.
Three kings dead at the battle of Wadi al-Makhazin. Ahmad al-Mansur is sultan.
The sultan's army has crossed the Sahara and beaten the Songhai at Tondibi.
Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur is dead of the plague.
Sonni Ali's horsemen have taken Timbuktu.
Askia Muhammad rules the Songhai.
Askia Muhammad has set out for Mecca on pilgrimage, with a great train.
Askia Muhammad, old and blind, has been set aside by his son.
Askia Dawud rules the Songhai. Scholars come from far to Timbuktu.
Moroccan musketeers have beaten the Songhai at Tondibi. Gao has fallen.
The Moroccan pasha has arrested the scholars of Timbuktu.
Sultan Qaitbay rules from the Citadel.
The sultan Qansuh al-Ghawri builds his great mosque and market.
Sultan al-Ghawri is dead at Marj Dabiq, fighting the Ottomans.
Tumanbay, the last Mamluk sultan, is put to death at the Zuwayla gate.
Strange ships with white sails at the mouth of the river.
King Nzinga a Nkuwu is baptised, as João.
Afonso is king of Kongo after a battle for the throne.
King Afonso opens a school for the sons of the nobles.
King Afonso has written to Portugal to protest the trade in people.
Raiders from the east have burned Mbanza Kongo. The king has fled.
The Portuguese have founded a town at Luanda.
Mbanza Kongo, now São Salvador, has its own bishop.
Portuguese soldiers march on Ndongo with Imbangala allies.
Nzinga, sister of the ngola, has gone to Luanda to talk peace.
Nzinga rules Ndongo.
Queen Nzinga rules from Matamba.
The Dutch have taken Luanda.
The Portuguese are back in Luanda.

A merchant's mule train came in from Bologna.
The guilds walked in procession for their saint.

Corsairs were seen off the coast. The watch towers lit their fires.
Grain ships came in from the south.

The watch took a cutpurse at the fair.
A ship came in with wine from Bordeaux.
iberia: Silk merchants came in from the Alpujarras.

A caravan came in from Sijilmasa with gold.
The Qarawiyyin's scholars debated late into the night.
sahel: A salt caravan came in from Taghaza.
The scholars of Sankore copied new books.
The river is high. The boats come and go to Djenné.
egypt: The muhtasib fined a cloth seller for short measures.
The Nile flood was good. Grain is cheaper.
Pilgrims gathered for the caravan to Mecca.
kongo: Traders came in from the coast with cloth.
The market was full of raffia cloth and salt.

quiet: A quiet year. The river rose, then fell again.
The year went by between the market and the prayers.
Nothing the criers would cry, but a good year at home.

events.text: The feast of San Giovanni. Banners hang from every window, and the palio horses run bareback through the streets.

choices.label: Watch the palio
choices.outcome: You squeezed to the front. The Albizzi horse won, and the crowd nearly carried you away.

choices.label: Bet a soldo on a horse
choices.outcome: Your horse threw its rider at the first corner. You learned something about betting.

events.text: Your father wants you at the abacus school, to learn reckoning for trade. It costs a florin a year.

choices.label: Go and learn your numbers
choices.outcome: You learned to reckon interest and exchange like a merchant's son.

flags.abacus: learning reckoning at the abacus school

choices.label: Stay home and help instead
choices.outcome: You stayed and helped. Your hands grew rough before your head grew learned.

events.text: A master of the Arte della Lana needs carders for his shop by the river.

choices.label: Take the work
choices.outcome: The work was hard and the wool got everywhere, but there were florins at the end of the year.

choices.label: Look for better
choices.outcome: You held out for something better. It did not come this year.

events.text: A marriage broker comes to the house. A family two streets over has a match in mind, and a dowry of 150 florins is spoken of.

choices.label: Agree to the match
choices.outcome: The notary drew up the contract and the families shook hands in church.

choices.label: Refuse for now
choices.outcome: The broker left in a huff. Your mother did not speak to you for a week.

events.text: Friar Savonarola preaches in the Duomo that Florence must burn its vanities. Boys in white go door to door collecting mirrors and paintings.

choices.label: Give them your finery
choices.outcome: You handed over a mirror and a painted chest. The friar's boys sang as they carried them off.

choices.label: Bar the door
choices.outcome: You kept your things and your door shut. Someone chalked a cross on it in the night.

events.text: Young men are playing calcio in the Piazza Santa Croce. A team is one player short.

choices.label: Join in
choices.outcome: You scored once and lost a tooth. Worth it.

choices.label: Watch from the steps
choices.outcome: You watched and shouted with the rest.

notes.text: Since 1516 the Jews of Venice live in the Ghetto, locked at night.
Since 1555 the Jews of Rome live in a walled ghetto by the river.
The Jews of Fez live in the mellah, the quarter by the royal palace.
The law asks everyone to come to church on Sunday. Those who keep the old faith are called recusants and pay fines.
The Crown has changed the church more than once in your lifetime.

ventures.lost: The galleys were taken by pirates off Brittany.

ventures.label: A share in a cloth shipment to Antwerp
ventures.about: Florentine cloth north, back next year
ventures.lost: The bales rotted in a wet hold off Marseille.

ventures.label: A share in a Por Santa Maria silk shop
ventures.lost: The shop failed, and its partners fled their debts.

ventures.label: A share in the spice galleys to Alexandria
ventures.about: Pepper and cloves for Venice, back next year
ventures.lost: A Turkish squadron took the galleys.

ventures.label: A share in a grain ship from Sicily
ventures.lost: The ship went down in a winter storm.

ventures.label: A share in the papal alum mines at Tolfa

ventures.lost: The alum sat unsold in the warehouses all year.

ventures.label: A share in a Milanese armourer's shop
ventures.about: Helmets and breastplates for every army
ventures.lost: The buyer was killed in battle, and never paid.

ventures.label: A share in a Portuguese cargo from the Indies

ventures.lost: The carrack was lost off the Cape of Good Hope.

ventures.label: A share in the cloth fleet to Antwerp
ventures.about: English broadcloth across the sea, back next year
ventures.lost: The cloth fleet was seized in a quarrel with the Netherlands.

ventures.label: A subscription to an East India voyage
ventures.about: Ships of the East India Company, out and back in two years
ventures.lost: The ships did not come back.

ventures.label: Shares in the Dutch East India Company (VOC)
ventures.about: Bought through an agent on the Amsterdam exchange
ventures.lost: The VOC paid no dividend this year, and the price fell.

ventures.label: A qirad share in a caravan across the Sahara
ventures.about: You give the money, a merchant gives the work: you share the profit and the loss
ventures.lost: The caravan lost its way, and the camels with it.

ventures.label: A qirad share in the Red Sea spice trade
ventures.lost: The Portuguese took the ship in the Red Sea.

ventures.label: A share in a copper and cloth caravan
ventures.about: Copper from the north, raffia cloth to the coast
ventures.lost: The caravan was robbed on the road to the coast.

list.about: Fields, a well and a walled garden. Far from the plague

list.label: A mud-brick house
list.about: Thick walls, a roof terrace, cool at night

list.label: A scholar's house with a library
list.about: Manuscripts in chests, students at the door

list.label: A great compound
list.about: Courtyards for a household, horses and guests

list.label: A house in your lineage's compound
list.about: Wattle walls and a thatch, kin all around

list.label: A walled compound
list.about: Your own enclosure of woven walls, with a courtyard

list.label: A noble's enclosure
list.about: A maze of walls near the court, with clients and guards

list.label: A kilombo war camp
list.about: A fortified camp of warriors who follow you
list.lock: For a war leader of noble birth

legend.label: A room above Verrocchio's workshop
legend.about: Sawdust, plaster and bronze filings; the master's pupils on the stair

legend.label: The vineyard by San Vittore
legend.about: Sixteen perches of vines outside Milan, a gift of Ludovico Sforza
legend.gift: Ludovico gives you a vineyard outside the Porta Vercellina: sixteen perches of vines, yours to keep.

legend.label: The manor of Cloux at Amboise
legend.about: A red-brick manor near the king's château, with a pension
legend.gift: Francis I gives you the manor of Cloux at Amboise, a short walk from his château, and a pension of a thousand écus a year.

items.about: Good cloth from the Arte della Lana

items.label: A wool burnous
items.about: A hooded cloak against the cold nights

items.label: Imported cloth from the coast
items.about: European linen and silk, a mark of rank at court

items.label: A horse
items.about: Rare and costly here: a mark of the powerful

items.about: From a stationer by St Paul's

items.about: For drawing and notes

items.about: Carry it by day. After curfew it's still a crime

items.label: A pound of pepper
items.about: For a feast, or to sell on

activities.label: Carnival
activities.about: Masks, floats and songs before Lent
activities.good: You danced behind the floats until dawn, mask on, nobody's son.
activities.bad: A mask came off at the wrong moment. Everyone saw who you were with.

activities.label: The feast of San Giovanni
activities.about: The procession, the offerings and the palio
activities.good: You cheered the palio horses home from the best spot on the Corso.
activities.bad: Crushed in the crowd, you saw nothing but backs.

activities.label: Walk in a procession
activities.about: Corpus Domini: banners, candles and the whole city
activities.good: You carried a candle with your confraternity, in step all the way.
activities.bad: Your candle went out in the wind halfway round.

activities.label: Walk in a procession
activities.about: Corpus Christi and the guild pageants
activities.good: You walked behind your guild's banner as the pageant wagons rolled.
activities.bad: Rain soaked the pageant and the banners ran.

activities.label: The Mawlid procession
activities.about: Lamps, poems and sweets for the Prophet's birthday
activities.good: You walked with the lamps and the singers until late.
activities.bad: The crowd was so thick you went home early.

activities.label: Calcio in Santa Croce
activities.about: Twenty-seven a side, and almost no rules
activities.good: You carried the ball through three tacklers and scored. The square roared.
activities.bad: You took a fist to the jaw in the first minute.

activities.label: Watch a joust
activities.about: Knights in the lists, lances and a crowd
activities.good: A lance shattered right in front of you. You kept a splinter.
activities.bad: The best knight was unhorsed early, and the day fizzled out.

activities.label: Ride in the joust
activities.about: Armour, a lance and your house's colours
activities.good: Your lance broke clean on his shield. The ladies' stand rose.
activities.bad: You were unhorsed and lay in the sand, seeing stars.

activities.label: Pallacorda
activities.about: Tennis on a walled court, for a wager
activities.good: You won the set and the wager.
activities.bad: You lost the set, the wager and your temper.

activities.label: Real tennis
activities.about: Tennis on an indoor court, the king's own game
activities.good: You won the set and the wager.
activities.bad: You lost the set and the wager.

activities.label: Cards and dice
activities.about: Primiera at the tavern. Dice are forbidden
activities.good: You won a few coins and a reputation.
activities.bad: You lost what you'd put down, and then some.

activities.label: Chess in the coffee courtyard
activities.about: Shatranj with an old man who never loses
activities.good: You beat him at last. He bought the tea.
activities.bad: He beat you in twelve moves and told everyone.

activities.label: The tavern
activities.about: Wine, stories and quarrels
activities.good: A good night: songs, stories and a new friend.
activities.bad: A drunk picked a fight with you over nothing.

activities.label: The storytellers' square
activities.about: Tales of Antar and the Thousand and One Nights
activities.good: You stayed for the whole tale of Antar, and paid the teller twice.
activities.bad: Rain broke up the circle before the end.

activities.label: The stufa
activities.about: The bathhouse: steam, gossip and a barber
activities.good: You came out light as air.
activities.bad: The water was dirty and the barber was drunk.

activities.label: The bathhouse
activities.about: The stews on the Bankside, before the King shuts them
activities.good: Hot water and a long soak.
activities.bad: The water was cold and the company was worse.

activities.label: The hammam
activities.about: Hot rooms, cold water and the scrub
activities.good: You came out scrubbed, steamed and new.
activities.bad: Too hot for too long: you came out dizzy.

activities.label: Sing with the lute
activities.about: Frottole and songs at a friend's house
activities.good: Your song made the whole room go quiet.
activities.bad: You lost the tune in the second verse.

activities.label: Lute and madrigals
activities.about: Five voices round a table, the parts on one book
activities.good: Your voice held the part to the end.
activities.bad: You came in a bar early, twice.

activities.label: Songs and the lute
activities.about: Ballads and part-songs after supper
activities.good: Everyone joined the last chorus.
activities.bad: A string snapped mid-song.

activities.label: The oud and the nuba
activities.about: The old music of al-Andalus, suite by suite
activities.good: The players let you take a verse.
activities.bad: You lost the mode and the players frowned.

activities.label: Griots and drums
activities.about: The griot sings the deeds of the old kings
activities.good: The griot sang your family's name.
activities.bad: The drummers left early.

activities.label: Dance at the court
activities.about: Drums, ivory horns and the mani watching
activities.good: You danced until the drummers tired. The court noticed you.
activities.bad: You missed the turn and the court laughed.

activities.label: Ride out and hunt
activities.about: Hounds, a hawk and the hills
activities.good: A long gallop and a hare for supper.
activities.bad: Your horse shied at a ditch and you went over its head.

activities.label: The market
activities.about: Cloth, beasts, books and everything else

activities.label: Pilgrimage to Rome
activities.about: The jubilee year: every sin forgiven at St Peter's
activities.good: You walked to Rome, knelt at St Peter's and came home changed.
activities.bad: Fever on the road. You reached Rome, but barely.

activities.label: A pilgrimage
activities.about: To Loreto or Assisi, on foot
activities.good: You reached the shrine and left a candle.
activities.bad: Blisters, rain and a robbed purse.

activities.label: A pilgrimage to Canterbury
activities.about: To Becket's shrine, until the King destroys it
activities.good: You reached Becket's shrine and bought a pilgrim's badge.
activities.bad: The inns were full and the road was mud.

activities.label: The hajj
activities.about: With the caravan to Mecca: once in a life, if you can
activities.title: hajji
activities.good: You stood at Arafat with a hundred thousand others. You come home a hajji.
activities.bad: The caravan suffered on the road, but you reached Mecca.

activities.label: The playhouse
activities.about: A penny to stand in the yard
activities.good: The whole yard wept at the death scene. So did you.
activities.bad: A pickpocket worked the yard while you watched.

activities.label: The night streets
activities.about: Curfew, blades, dice and the drum

activities.label: Make a journey
activities.about: Another city, by road, sea or caravan

houses.note: Fortunes are historians' estimates in gold florins, shown in the money of where you live; the list follows history unless your life changes it.

list.name: The Pazzi
list.fallen: Ruined and banished after their plot, April 1478

notes.1520: Agostino dies, the richest man in Rome

list.name: The Aqit
list.fallen: Exiled to Marrakesh after the Moroccan conquest

list.name: The households of the Mamluk emirs
list.fallen: Swept away by the Ottoman conquest, 1517

phlegmatic.label: Phlegmatic
phlegmatic.about: calm and patient, slow to change

minds.text: The harvest failed and there's little to eat. {they} won't ask you for help.
{they_cap} owes money to a lender and lies awake over it.
A cough that won't go away this winter.
Lonely since the last time you came.
Worried about a match for a daughter: there's no dowry.
Looking for work, and too proud to say so.
Afraid of the plague this year.
In love with someone the family won't accept.

good: Ha! You always know how to cheer a house.
Come again, and bring friends next time!
Now that's a day worth telling about.
bad: You've gone sour, you know that?

good: At last someone in this family talks sense.
bad: Don't tell me what to think.
You've a nerve, after all I've done.

good: I'll keep this, you know. I keep everything.
bad: You always did leave too soon.

good: Well. That was a good day.

mother.old: You drew the river on the wall with a burnt stick. Your grandfather beat the wall, not you.
mother.secret: Some things a mother keeps. Ask your father, if you dare.

leonardo.father: Ask why you can't be a notary
